newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says Israel fabricating military problem.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says Israel fabricating military problem.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Sunday accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of trying to create a problem over routine manoeuvres by the Egyptian armed forces.
"Netanyahu wants to fabricate a problem and I never imagined he would do that," Mubarak told reporters after his military commanders briefed him on 10 days of manoeuvres.
"If he had any anxiety, he could have contacted us and we could have spoken openly," he added.

Mubarak said he had heard Israeli statements of concern about the exercise and especially over the codename Badr, the name of the first battle by the army of the Prophet Mohammad, fought in AD 624 against the polytheists of Mecca.
Israeli media said last week that Netanyahu's defence establishment had been debating the significance of the Egyptian exercises, the largest since 1993.

Egyptian Defence Minister Mohamed Hussein Tantawi has also said the exercises included training on how to deal with nuclear attack. Israel's alleged nuclear arsenal is one of Egypt's biggest security concerns.
Netanyahu referred to both the Egyptian manoeuvres and Syrian troop movements, saying: "We must stand determined here, follow with caution any movement of forces."
But Mubarak said the manoeuvres were just defensive training exercises of the kind any country holds from time to time.

"I am surprised (at reports of Israeli concern)," he said. "The exercises were called Badr in 1993 in the days of (Israeli prime minister Yitzhak) Rabin...What is there to upset them? They weren't upset before."
"I want to say that there is a peace treaty between us and Israel and we respect our treaty fully," he added.

The manoeuvres, which ended last week, featured combined operations by the army, navy and air force. One night they carried out a crossing of the Suez Canal from west to east, similar to the operation which launched war on Israel in 1973.

Mubarak's remarks are part of a war of words that has intensified since Netanyahu said last week that Egypt, by threatening to postpone a Middle East economic conference in November, was like someone cutting off his nose to spite his face.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa retorted that Netanyahu should keep off Egypt's nose if he wanted to protect his own.

Egyptian officials and government newspapers have been attacking Netanyahu daily for his attempts to steer Middle East peace talks away from the principle that Israel will give back Arab land in exchange for peace.
In an interview with the German magazine Der Spiegel Mubarak said bluntly that Netanyahu had broken a promise to respect all the agreements made by the previous Israeli government.
A foreign ministry undersecretary, Adel el-Safty, also said on Sunday that only a psychiatrist could help Netanyahu overcome an obsession with Israel's security.
"The Israeli prime minister...(has) a pathological fear on the security issue, which cannot be solved on the negotiating table but only by a psychiatrist," he said.
